name: swftools
why: Tools for dissecting and generating Flash SWF files open a door into an obsolete binary format with a lot of hidden structure.

brief.what_it_is: SWFTools is a collection of command-line utilities for Adobe Flash SWF files. Some programs read and inspect existing SWFs (swfdump, swfstrings, swfextract, swfbbox), some combine or rewrite them (swfcombine), and others build new SWFs from images, sound, PDFs, fonts, or ActionScript source (pdf2swf, png2swf, jpeg2swf, gif2swf, wav2swf, font2swf, swfc, as3compile). The README lists the tools by name with one-line descriptions and does not show a full usage example.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a toolkit for working with Flash files: reading SWFs, combining them, and creating them from other content such as images, sound files, videos or source code. It does not state a broader motivation.
brief.how_it_works: Each executable is a separate tool with a narrow job, such as dumping contents, extracting movieclips, sounds and images, or converting one input format into an SWF. The README says PDF2SWF is based on the xpdf PDF parser by Derek B. Noonburg, and WAV2SWF uses the L.A.M.E. MP3 encoder library. The README does not describe internal architecture further.
brief.install_notes: The README gives no build or install steps beyond the project's own description. It lists supported platforms as Solaris, Linux (32 and 64 bit), FreeBSD, OpenBSD, HP-UX, MacOS X and Windows 98/ME/2000/XP/Vista. The brew metadata lists 11 executables: as3compile, font2swf, png2swf, swfbbox, swfc, swfcombine, swfdump, swfextract, swfrender, swfstrings, wav2swf. Note that pdf2swf, jpeg2swf and gif2swf appear in the README but not in the brew executable list, and swfrender is in the brew list but not described in the README.
brief.standout: The SWF format is obsolete, and these tools are one of the few complete open-source toolchains that can both take apart and generate SWF files. swfdump's disassembly, cross-reference and bounding-box output exposes a lot of the format's internal structure, which the scout notes point to as the main draw.
brief.status: unknown. The fetched README gives no release date, last commit, or version number. One note in the README says AVI2SWF was removed from the latest version because ffmpeg or mencoder do the job better, which suggests the project has been pruned but does not date it.
brief.caveats: The README is the only source read, so the install process, licensing details beyond 'GPL', and current build status are unverified. Adobe Flash is discontinued, so the output SWFs have limited modern playback. The README's platform list reaches back to Windows 98 and HP-UX, so it may be dated. The brew executable list and the README tool list do not fully match.
quotes: SWFTools is a collection of utilities for working with Adobe Flash files (SWF files).
The tool collection includes programs for reading SWF files, combining them, and creating them from other content (like images, sound files, videos or sourcecode).
SWFTools is released under the GPL.
